judged_text: Attendees are committed to the database (prisma.booking.update createMany) before updateCalendarAttendees and email sending run, with no rollback or compensation if either later step throws. If eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees throws (bad credential, calendar API error), the request 500s but the guests rows are already persisted; the calendar event never gains the guests and no email is sent, while the database says they were added — silent partial state with no retry path, since a retry hits the duplicate-filter and returns BAD_REQUEST.

record.issue_text: [BUG] Attendees are committed to the database (prisma.booking.update createMany) before updateCalendarAttendees and email sending run, with no rollback or compensation if either later step throws. If eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees throws (bad credential, calendar API error), the request 500s but the guests rows are already persisted; the calendar event never gains the guests and no email is sent, while the database says they were added — silent partial state with no retry path, since a retry hits the duplicate-filter and returns BAD_REQUEST.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the handler persists new attendee rows first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` and then attempts email sending. There is no transaction/rollback or compensating logic if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (it is not wrapped in try/catch). In that failure case, the request will error after the DB has been updated, leaving guests stored in Prisma but not applied to the external calendar and (since execution stops) no emails sent. A retry will compute `uniqueGuests` by filtering out existing attendees and can hit `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and throw BAD_REQUEST, matching the finding’s “no retry path” claim.
